appraisal_events.evidence: « Saint-Loup pourrait ce qu'il voudrait sur Monserfeuil. Seulement, comme il ne sait pas ce qu'il veut, il le fait demander par nous, parce qu'il sait qu'il n'y a pas de meilleure manière de faire échouer la chose. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The duke concedes Saint-Loup has real influence with Monserfeuil but faults him as indecisive and portrays his choice to route the request through others as ensuring its failure; the narrator has just flagged this whole speech as a self-serving maneuver by the duke, so the blame is unreliable.

status_effects.explanation: The duke's characterization casts Saint-Loup's request as ill-considered and self-defeating, weakening its standing, though this reading comes from a narrator-flagged self-interested speaker.

ambiguities: The duke's remarks about Saint-Loup occur within a speech the narrator explicitly frames as strategic self-justification (to deflect blame from the duchess onto his own temper and onto Saint-Loup's indecision), so it is unclear how much of this characterization reflects genuine assessment versus rhetorical convenience.

Princesse de Parme was considered as a candidate but omitted: she relays and then withdraws the request and changes the subject, but the passage gives her no distinct evaluative outcome of her own beyond facilitating the already-scored duchess/duke interaction.
